reachable: Yes, for both new mechanisms, with one structural exception. HEAD: the registry's injection is gated by rd_active = vc (command validity only), and the transport's contrib carries no validity gate at all — so at the scoring layout, where the read command is valid and its observation is key-padded, both contributions are LIVE at the read. This is the failure mode the brief warned about (a mechanism gated on the observation being present), and this candidate does not have it: only the WRITE paths use vc & vo. Measured: injecting nonzero out_scale changes the prediction at the read position by 6.44 / 2.84 (L2-sum) for windows below the batch-global max r, and by exactly 0 for the window at max r (see divergence 1). Gradient: in a real 8-step H._train run on synthetic sequences both out_scale vectors moved off zero (0.0313 and 0.0283) and the registry aux was nonzero and rising each step, so both memories receive gradient through the main loss and at least the registry through its aux. OPTIM: both mechanisms act on the parameters that are handed to the instrument, verified by execution — the returned net's parameters equal the mean of the constant-LR tail iterates to 1e-7 (not the last iterate), and every gradient consumed after step 160 was measured at a point displaced by exactly 5% of each 2-D layer's Frobenius norm along the previous step's gradient, with the displaced loss higher in 10/10 checks. No displacement survives the final step (finalize returns before _displace), so the scored net is undisplaced, averaged and spectrally re-capped.
solves_outside_model: No. This is the cleanest part of the candidate. Neither the optim nor either head touches command text: I grepped all four files for cmds / .split( / re. / str( and the only string operation in the whole candidate is `k.startswith(\"reg_\"/\"trn_\")` on genome PARAMETER names in _split_params. Both memories operate purely on the frozen embedding tensors and both write only into `pred` (registry returns pred + add; transport returns pred.clone() with an added slice) — neither modifies tok_emb, so nothing resolved reaches the model as input. The auxiliaries mine positions from embedding distances and shape a loss; that is the legitimate kind. The optim only reads gradients and parameters. There is no path resembling the retracted stream shortcut. One inherited note, not new here and not a shortcut: the registry's InfoNCE candidate bank is masked by `valid` rather than by \"seen so far\", so future observations act as negatives in the training loss — a train-time-only use of future info that never runs at eval (aux is skipped outside training mode).
summary: The code does what the hypothesis says. I checked the numeric claims by execution rather than reading, and they hold literally: the composed forward is bit-identical to the bare arch at initialisation (maxdiff exactly 0.0, both out_scale vectors zero-init); the two wraps chain in the stated order with disjoint attributes, stashes and parameter sets (registry 322,630 params, transport 932,611); both auxiliaries are invoked and summed with the transport's aux_weight forced to 0.5; the displacement is exactly rho*||w|| per 2-D parameter (measured 0.05000 at every step), is measured at the previous step's gradient direction, is subtracted before the update so decay/cap/averaging see undisplaced weights, and touches no 1-D or 0-D parameter (pos_scale and logit_decay exist and are 0-dim, out_scale is 1-D); the tail average is genuinely written back (final params equal the tail mean to 1e-7, and differ from the last iterate by ~4e-3); the schedule reaches the 0.12 floor exactly at the tail start and holds it (warm 160, decay 1360->3000, 1001 accumulations at steps=4000); Muon picks up rename_registry.addr_a/addr_b (64,192) alongside the arch's six (64,176) projections under the inherited shape+sibling rule, and the spectral cap lands on tr_read.weight (768,768). The data claim also checks out: all 172 mv steps in evolve/jail_data/train_sample.jsonl have output == \"\". Crucially, the mechanism is not switched off at the read: both memories gate only their WRITE path on the observation being present, and their read injection is gated on command validity or not at all, so both are live at the scored position — I confirmed this by building the exact scoring layout and measuring the prediction delta at rpos. The one structural limit worth recording is that n = L//2 drops the last command of an odd-length sequence, so the window(s) at the batch-global maximum r get zero head contribution at their read; this is inherited unchanged from both parent heads and affects a small minority of windows. The remaining divergences are wording (\"exact restore\" is 3e-8, not bit-exact; SAM's warmup gate is unstated) plus an unflagged activation-memory cost from running two recurrent memories at once.

divergences.claim: "Both inject their read at command positions ... so the composed forward is exactly the bare arch forward at initialisation" — implying the read at the scored position is influenced by both memories.
divergences.what_the_code_does: Both heads compute n = L//2. The scoring layout is odd-length (Lmax = 2*max(r)+1), so n = max(r) and the covered command positions are 0,2,...,2*max(r)-2. For the window(s) whose r equals the batch-global maximum, the read position 2r = 2*max(r) falls OUTSIDE the injected range and receives exactly zero contribution from either memory. All shorter windows are covered normally. Measured on a mixed batch rs=[3,4,6]: delta at read = 6.4355, 2.8397, 0.0000. Inherited identically from both parent heads (r3_rename_registry, r2_dualaddress), not introduced here; the sampled slice suggests a small minority of windows (2/24 in evolve/jail_data/train_sample.jsonl sit at max r, and the real slice has far more windows sharing one global max).
divergences.evidence: evolve/chunks/head/r3_rename_registry_occupancy_routing.py:117 (n = L // 2) and :218 (n = min(contrib.size(1), pred.size(1) // 2)); evolve/chunks/head/r2_dualaddress_move_transport.py:107 and :176-179. Executed against the real genome with the exact build_cups_layout shape (evolve/cups_probe.py:105-129).

divergences.claim: "w <- w - e_t (exact restore of the stored tensor)"
divergences.what_the_code_does: p.data.add_(e) then p.data.sub_(e) in fp32 — measured residual 2.98e-08 max abs over a 30-step run, i.e. round-off, not bit-exact. Harmless in magnitude but the word "exact" is an overstatement.

divergences.claim: Section 2(a) describes the displacement as unconditional ("end of step t: w <- w + e_t").
divergences.what_the_code_does: Displacement is additionally gated on t >= sam_start, and sam_start is set to `warm` (160 of 4000 steps with this genome). SAM is therefore inert through warmup. This is a sensible detail but is nowhere stated in the hypothesis.
divergences.evidence: evolve/chunks/optim/r4_flatbasin_lsam_tailavg.py:212 and :291-293 (sam_start=warm); measured sam_start=160, avg_start=3000, steps=4000 for the genome's params.

divergences.claim: Speed is flagged as the only unmeasured cost ("none of it changes the step budget, only wall-clock per step").
divergences.what_the_code_does: Running both recurrent memories also doubles the retained activation footprint: the transport keeps a B x 48 x 768 state per step and the registry a B x 16 x 768 content matrix per step, both kept in the graph across n steps. At bs=64 and n~31 that is roughly 400 MB of fp32 activations from the two memories alone, on top of the trunk. Memory is not mentioned in the failure-modes section. Measured forward+backward cost on CPU (B=16, n=31): bare 237 ms, +registry 253 ms, +transport 228 ms, composite 305 ms (~+29% vs bare, aux mining excluded).
divergences.evidence: evolve/chunks/head/r2_dualaddress_move_transport.py:134-146 (mem via baddbmm in a loop); r3_rename_registry_occupancy_routing.py:146-184 (addr/cont/fill in a loop). Timing measured on this machine.
